newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends up after oil sales.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends up after oil sales.

text.p: *Oil firms to buy $38 million on Wednesday
The Philippine peso finished up on Tuesday at 26.345 against the dollar from 26.349 after banks met the $31-million requirement of oil companies, traders said.
The day's average was also at a higher 26.347 from 26.349. Volume narrowed to $136.50 million from $138.05 million.
"The oils were done at 26.348 when the market was doing at 26.349," a foreign bank dealer said.
That helped the peso regain ground despite earlier hitting a low of 26.35, a dealer said.
Sales to oil companies are done outside the formal, computerised foreign exchange market among banks.
Traders also said the Central Bank made its presence known in the market by quoting bid and rates for the dollar at 26.29/26.35.
"The dollar's bounce could be bigger on Wednesday," a trader said, since oil companies are scheduled to buy a further $38 million.
